cases.customer_question: Can an existing Bluetooth-qualified TV platform reuse prior RF and lower-layer qualification assets after an OS version update while limiting new testing to updated profiles?
question_variants: Can we reuse existing RF/RF-PHY reports for an OS update?
Does an Android or OS version change require full Bluetooth requalification?
Can prior QDID layers be inherited without retesting?
How do we avoid LL retesting when only profile versions changed?
Can A2DP and AVRCP updates be qualified independently?
cases.actual_issue: The product reused an existing Bluetooth hardware platform and previously qualified Design, but updated software and profile versions created uncertainty about whether full lower-layer retesting would be triggered under QPRDv3/QPRDv4.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The customer changed software and some Bluetooth profile versions on an existing TV platform but did not change the radio hardware. They wanted to avoid repeating expensive Bluetooth testing that had already been completed for the previous product generation. The key challenge was selecting the correct Qualification Workspace approach so that only the changed Bluetooth functions required new testing.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant determined that RF and RF-PHY reports could be reused because the hardware and RF behavior were unchanged. The recommended approach was to create a compatible subset or modified Design using the existing qualification assets while limiting ICS changes to the layers that truly changed. The consultant explained that modifying A2DP and AVRCP profile versions would still trigger profile-level testing and report uploads, but unnecessary LL and RF retesting could be avoided if lower-layer ICS settings remained unchanged and consistent. The consultant also emphasized maintaining consistency-check compliance and minimizing inter-layer dependency impacts.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth qualification scope is driven by ICS changes, layer inheritance, inter-layer dependencies, and TCRL applicability. If RF and lower-layer implementations remain unchanged, existing evidence can be reused, but profile version changes requiring ICS modifications generate mandatory testing for the modified layers.
cases.final_recommendation: Reuse the previously qualified RF and lower-layer Design assets, create a subset or compatible Design in Qualification Workspace, modify only the required A2DP and AVRCP profile layers, and execute only the resulting mandatory profile-level testing.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrect Design inheritance or unnecessary ICS modifications could trigger large-scale lower-layer test plans, including approximately 300 LL-related upload requirements. Improper layer selection could also force unnecessary RF, RF-PHY, or interoperability testing, increasing qualification cost and schedule risk.
